explanation: Use grade-school multiplication on the absolute decimal digits. Accumulate each digit product in its positional slot and carry to the preceding slot. Remove leading zeros and put the combined sign on the first digit only.
timeComplexity: O(mn) time for m and n digits.
spaceComplexity: O(m + n) space for the product digits.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Each pair of decimal digits contributes its product to the corresponding place value. Processing from least significant positions stores the remainder in that digit and carries the quotient to the next position. After every pair is included, trimming zeros and applying the combined sign yields the same integer product.
walkthrough: [-1,3] represents −13 and [2,4] represents 24. The absolute digit multiplication produces 312; the signs differ, so return [-3,1,2].
edgeCases: Only the first digit carries the sign.
Any product equal to zero is returned as [0], without a negative sign.
Long digit arrays are multiplied directly instead of being parsed into a fixed-width integer.
